title: Make Your Resume ATS-Friendly
tips: Use standard section headings: 'Work Experience', 'Education', 'Skills', 'Projects', 'Certifications'.
Mirror keywords from the job description — if the JD says 'REST API development', use 'REST API development' not 'API building'.
Avoid tables, text boxes, columns, headers/footers, and graphics — ATS parsers cannot read these reliably.
Use a clean single-column format for ATS submissions; decorative two-column resumes are for human-only review.
Save as PDF (universally safe) or .docx (if employer specifies). Avoid .pages, .odt formats.
Include the job title in your resume (e.g., 'Applying for: Software Engineer at XYZ') subtly.
Quantify achievements: '↑ performance by 40%' beats 'improved performance'.
Keep file name professional: 'YourName_Resume_SoftwareEngineer.pdf' not 'resume_final_v3_new.pdf'.

title: Ideal Resume Structure for Fresh Engineering Graduates
tips: Order: Contact Info → Summary/Objective → Education → Skills → Projects → Internships/Experience → Certifications → Achievements.
Keep resume to 1 page for freshers, 2 pages for 3+ years experience.
Contact Info: Name (large, bold), Email, Phone, LinkedIn URL, GitHub URL, City (not full address).
Summary: 2–3 lines. Example: 'Final year B.Tech CSE student with hands-on experience in Java Spring Boot and React. Built 3 full-stack projects. Seeking SDE role in product company.'
Education: University Name, Degree (B.Tech CSE), Year of passing, CGPA (if above 7.0).
Skills: Categorise — Programming Languages | Frameworks & Libraries | Databases | Tools & Platforms.
Projects: Project Name | Tech Stack used | 2–3 bullet points describing what it does, your role, and impact/result.
Never include photo, date of birth, religion, marital status, or father's name (standard in modern tech resumes).

title: How to Write the Skills Section
tips: Don't rate your skills (avoid: 'Python ★★★★☆'). Just list them — rating yourself poorly is a red flag, rating yourself perfectly seems dishonest.
Categorise skills: Programming Languages, Frameworks, Databases, Tools, Cloud, Soft Skills (optional).
Only list skills you can actually discuss in an interview. Listing 'Machine Learning' when you've only done one tutorial is dangerous.
Include both technical and relevant soft skills (e.g., 'Team Collaboration, Agile/Scrum' for product company roles).
Place most relevant skills first — tailor for each application.

title: Writing a Strong Projects Section
tips: Format: [Project Name] | [Tech Stack] | [GitHub Link]
3–5 bullet points per project. Start each with an action verb: Built, Designed, Implemented, Optimised, Deployed.
Include: (1) What the project does, (2) Your specific role, (3) Tech stack used, (4) Impact/result if available.
Example: 'Built a full-stack e-commerce platform using React, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL and deployed on AWS EC2. Implemented JWT authentication and Redis caching, reducing API response time by 35%.'
Prioritise projects with GitHub repos, live demos, or measurable outcomes.
Avoid listing college lab assignments — focus on personal, team, hackathon, or internship projects.

title: Top 10 Resume Mistakes to Avoid
tips: 1. Spelling and grammar errors — always proofread using Grammarly.
2. Using an unprofessional email (e.g., coolkid_123@gmail.com). Use firstname.lastname@gmail.com.
3. No GitHub link — for tech roles, this is almost mandatory.
4. Listing irrelevant skills (e.g., MS Paint, MS Word for a software engineer role).
5. Generic objective statement — tailor it to the specific role.
6. Inconsistent formatting — different fonts, sizes, bullet styles.
7. Including references ('References available on request') — wastes space, not needed.
8. Lying about skills or experience — you will be tested.
9. Not updating resume for each application — tailoring increases shortlist probability by 40–60%.
10. File larger than 2MB — compress PDF if needed.
